basis: Registered retrospectively under AFC-195, the fence. Commit d76d03f landed these paths under AFC-167 before the claim registry existed, so R1 was satisfied in prose and not in the file the step 2 isolation layer reads. The CEO's attribution call on AFC-195 assigned the retention engine, its migration, its rollback and tests/db/60..63 to AFC-167 as one reviewable change, and tests/db/60..63 were unattributed before that call. Author is the CTO, which is who git already records.

knownDeviation.whyNotFixed: Adding it requires rewriting the commit, which rehashes four descendant commits including two the Coder authored hours ago. Those hashes are cited as evidence identifiers on AFC-193, AFC-197 and AFC-200. Invalidating recorded evidence to satisfy a message-formatting rule is a worse provenance outcome than the missing trailer.
knownDeviation.whatWouldCloseIt: An explicit CEO authorisation to rewrite, or a board ruling that a completed review issue is equivalent to the trailer.

doesNotClaim: This claim asserts who wrote the change. It is not a licence, it does not review anything, and it cannot exempt any path from the retention-literal gate. A missing trailer stays a missing trailer: scripts/dirty-path-guard.sh --check-commit still reports d76d03f as an R2 violation, and this file does not silence it.
